name: ckpt_restore
doc: DCP load: every rank reads .metadata, then the items of its shard file (fan-in `replicas`).

items.doc: read items per rank [config]; 900 for an 8B model

item_bytes.doc: [config] storage bytes of the item at each place in the file

item_off.doc: [config] the item's offset in the file: prefix sums of hdr + item_bytes + trailer - item_bytes mod 64, as §3 writes them

read_order.doc: [config] the place in the file of the k-th item read: the items sorted by name (layer.10 before layer.2), against the writer's state-dict order

replicas.doc: ranks that read the same shard file (replicated state saved once); 1 when fully sharded

meta_bytes.doc: [measure] .metadata size; traced 2,606 bytes for 6 items on 2 ranks

hdr.doc: per item, before the storage, as §3 writes it (traced 2026-10-01, torch 2.14)

trailer.doc: per item, after the storage, less the storage's length mod 64 (the next record is aligned), as §3 writes it

buf.doc: Python BufferedReader size = st_blksize; every buffer fill asks for this much

rec2.doc: offset in an item of its second zip record, where the reader goes after the central directory (traced)

eocd_scan.doc: the zip reader looks for the end record in the last 4096 bytes of an item

tail_back.doc: the item at the end of the file only: a fill there stops at EOF and is used up by the read that caused it, so each later step of the zip reader (end record, zip64 locator and record, central directory, the two records after the storage) is a fill of its own, this many bytes before the end (traced)
